newsitem.title: USA: Clark Blue Island, ILL. FCC remains down.
newsitem.headline: Clark Blue Island, ILL. FCC remains down.

text.p: Clark Refining & Marketing said Thursday that the fluid catalytic cracking (FCC) unit at its Blue Island, Illinois refinery will remain down until after a hearing to determine whether the plant should be completely closed on safety grounds.
The loss of the FCC means the plant is running at about 55,000 barrels-per-day (bpd), down from 72,000 bpd before a fire last Saturday and well below capacity of 80,515 bpd, a company spokesman said.

"We would have had the FCC back up by now but we have to wait for the (result) of the hearing," said Clark spokesman Syd Wiley, referring to a hearing in the Cook County Circuit Court in which the Illinois Attorney General is seeking to close the plant until the cause of a series of mishaps in the past two years can be determined.
The FCC unit requires the throughput from the propane "scrubber" unit, where last Saturday's fire occured.
The court hearing began on Wednesday and is set to resume on Friday.

In Thursday's session, the state argued that the plant should be shut pending a full investigation because of the "substantial danger" posed, particularly after incidents in which two employees were killed and where local high school children experienced lightheadedness after leaks.

Clark argues that the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency investigation is ongoing and will take weeks and it would be unfair to the company and its customers to close the entire plant until its results are in.
Clark is a unit of Clark USA Inc which is 46 pct owned by The Horsham Corp of Canada and 19 pct owned by Occidental Petroleum.
